description: Tackling the Lunar Landing Sight Navigator challenge
summary:
Lunar Skyline is an interactive web application that helps users explore and compare potential lunar landing sites using real lunar terrain and astronomical data.

Users can select locations directly on a 3D Moon, choose mission dates, and explore the local terrain through a first-person Skyline View. The application models Sun and Earth positions relative to the lunar horizon, helping users assess solar illumination and potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

Built using NASA LOLA elevation data, JPL SPICE ephemerides, React and Python, Lunar Skyline makes complex lunar mission-planning information more accessible to engineers, educators and the public.
details:
The problem

Selecting a lunar landing site requires understanding how terrain, sunlight and Earth visibility change with location and time. These factors are especially important near the lunar south pole, where crater walls and low solar angles can create prolonged shadowing and obstruct direct communication with Earth.

Existing scientific tools provide valuable data, but evaluating multiple candidate sites and dates can be difficult for non-specialists.

Our solution

Lunar Skyline brings lunar exploration and mission assessment into an interactive web application.

Users begin with a 3D Moon Explorer, select a proposed landing location directly on the lunar surface and specify a mission date and time. They can then enter Skyline View to explore the surrounding terrain and understand how the Sun and Earth appear relative to the local horizon.

The application supports comparing different candidate locations and observing how environmental conditions change over time.

Key capabilities

  • Interactive 3D lunar globe and custom landing-site selection.
  • First-person lunar terrain visualization.
  • Sun and Earth positioning calculated using JPL SPICE.
  • Terrain-aware horizon and obstruction analysis based on NASA LOLA elevation data.
  • Time-dependent visualization of illumination and celestial positions.
  • Mission assessment metrics for solar visibility and geometric direct-to-Earth line of sight.
  • Comparison of candidate landing-site scenarios.

Technology

The frontend uses React and Vite for interactive visualization. The backend uses Python and FastAPI to process lunar elevation data, generate terrain information and calculate celestial positions.

JPL SPICE provides astronomical ephemerides, while NASA LOLA supplies elevation information used to model the local lunar terrain and horizon.

Impact

Lunar Skyline helps users understand why landing-site selection is a balance between power availability, communication opportunities and terrain constraints. It offers a visual way to explore these trade-offs, supporting education and early-stage mission scenario evaluation.

Limitations and future development

The application is a preliminary planning and educational tool, not a flight-certified mission analysis system. Modelled solar visibility does not directly represent electrical power output, and geometric Earth line of sight does not guarantee a working communication link.

Future improvements could include more detailed engineering constraints, faster terrain-data delivery and expanded mission-analysis capabilities.
